io.github.thebusybiscuit.slimefun5.implementation.items.multiblocks

Class AbstractCraftingTable

  • java.lang.Object
    • io.github.thebusybiscuit.slimefun5.api.items.SlimefunItem
      • io.github.thebusybiscuit.slimefun5.core.multiblocks.MultiBlockMachine
        • io.github.thebusybiscuit.slimefun5.implementation.items.multiblocks.AbstractCraftingTable
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    ItemAttribute, NotPlaceable, Placeable, RecipeDisplayItem
    Direct Known Subclasses:
    ArmorForge, EnhancedCraftingTable, MagicWorkbench

    public abstract class AbstractCraftingTable
extends MultiBlockMachine
    This abstract super class is responsible for some utility methods for machines which are capable of upgrading backpacks.
    See Also:
    EnhancedCraftingTable, MagicWorkbench, ArmorForge

    • Method Detail

      • isCraftable

        protected abstract boolean isCraftable(org.bukkit.inventory.Inventory inv,
                                       org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack[] recipe)
        Whether the dispenser inventory matches the given recipe. Each crafting table implements this with its own matching rules (lore/backpack handling); the headless autoCraft(Block) reuses it.

      • isSlotLock

        protected static boolean isSlotLock(@Nullable
                                    org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack item)
        A SlimefunItems.SLOT_LOCK placed in a dispenser slot locks it, vanilla-Crafter style: the slot is treated as empty for recipe matching and is never consumed, while occupying the slot makes hoppers skip it. This returns whether the given item is such a lock marker.

      • ignoreLock

        @Nullable
protected static org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack ignoreLock(@Nullable
                                                                     org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack item)
        Returns null for a locked slot (so it matches an empty recipe cell), otherwise the item itself.

      • sameWoodMatch

        protected static boolean sameWoodMatch(@Nullable
                                       org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack slot,
                                       @Nullable
                                       org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack recipe)
        Whether a slot's plain vanilla wood satisfies a recipe cell of a different wood variant. Slimefun items are excluded (they still match strictly by id), so only plain wood is treated loosely.

      • consumeInputs

        protected void consumeInputs(@Nonnull
                             org.bukkit.inventory.Inventory inv)
        Consumes one of each non-lock input, mirroring a successful craft.

      • consumeInputs

        protected void consumeInputs(@Nonnull
                             org.bukkit.inventory.Inventory inv,
                             @Nonnull
                             org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack[] recipe)
        Consumes each input slot by the amount the matched recipe cell requires (not a hardcoded 1): recipes may need more than one of an ingredient per slot (e.g. 2 planks), and isCraftable already gates on slot.getAmount() >= recipe.getAmount(), so consuming only 1 left the surplus behind ("consumes one too little"). Slot-lock markers and empty recipe cells are skipped.

      • autoCraft

        public boolean autoCraft(@Nonnull
                         org.bukkit.block.Block dispenser)
        Performs a single craft headlessly (no Player, no permission check, no MultiBlockCraftEvent) directly from a powered dispenser, ejecting the result as a dropped item in the dispenser's facing direction. This backs the redstone auto-craft feature. Backpack recipes are skipped, since assigning a backpack requires a player.
        Overrides:
        autoCraft in class MultiBlockMachine
        Parameters:
        dispenser - The dispenser block that holds the recipe inputs
        Returns:
        Whether a craft was performed

      • getAutoCraftDelayTicks

        protected int getAutoCraftDelayTicks()
        Ticks a redstone auto-craft takes to complete before its output is ejected, mirroring the machine's manual craft time. 0 (default) ejects instantly (Enhanced Crafting Table); timed machines (Armor Forge, Magic Workbench) override this so redstone crafting takes as long as crafting by hand, and the dispenser cannot be re-powered until the current craft finishes.

      • getAutoCraftSoundSequence

        @Nonnull
protected java.util.List<AbstractCraftingTable.AutoCraftSoundStep> getAutoCraftSoundSequence()
        The ordered sound sequence a redstone auto-craft plays while it works, mirroring the machine's manual craft. The default is a single craft sound; timed machines (Armor Forge, Magic Workbench) override this with their full multi-step animation.

      • getAutoCraftSound

        @Nonnull
protected SoundEffect getAutoCraftSound()
        The single sound a redstone auto-craft plays by default (Enhanced Crafting Table). Timed machines instead override getAutoCraftSoundSequence() to play their full animation.

      • ejectOutput

        protected void ejectOutput(@Nonnull
                           org.bukkit.block.Block dispenser,
                           @Nonnull
                           org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack output)
        Ejects the crafted item out of the dispenser's front, exactly like a vanilla dispenser: spawned at the facing face, launched in that direction, with the dispenser dispense sound.
